text.p: Sunday's army takeover in Sierra Leone is the latest in a series of coups and coup attempts in the volatile West African state.
Following is a chronology of recent events:

April 29 - Soldiers led by Captain Valentine Strasser seize power, ousting civilian president Joseph Momoh, who goes into exile in Guinea. Coup inspired by frustration at war with rebels of the Revolutionary United Front, then just over a year old.
June - Security forces arrest three Britons accused of complicity in a coup plot. They are deported the following month.

December - Military government says it foiled coup attempt by Momoh loyalists, 26 people convicted of treason by a military tribunal are shot by firing squad on a beach near Freetown. Diplomats and rights groups say they suspect the coup story was invented as cover for a purge of Strasser's enemies.
March - Strasser government accuses Momoh of stockpiling weapons ready for an assault.
July - Strasser sacks his deputy, captain Solomon "Saj" Musa who takes refuge in the Nigerian high commissioner's residence fearing for his safety, then goes into exile in Britain.
November - Four British Asians arrested in Freetown and charged with conspiring with Musa to overthrow Strasser. They are released a year later.
October - Loyalist troops put down coup attempt while Strasser is abroad.

January - Officers led by Strasser's deputy Julius Maada Bio oust him in a palace coup. Strasser flies to Guinea and subsequently becomes a student in Britain. Bio agrees to go ahead with planned elections.
February 26 - First round of presidential and parliamentary elections disrupted by attacks by unidentified armed groups, particularly in Freetown and the southern town of Bo.
March 15 - Second round run-off won by lawyer Ahmad Tejan Kabbah with 59.5 percent of the vote
November 30 - Kabbah's government signs peace accord with Foday Sankoh's Revolutionary United Front.
March - Sankoh detained under effective house arrest in Nigeria.

March-May - Implementation of peace accord falls behind schedule. Troops clash with Kamajor hunter militias set up with Kabbah's support, while attacks in the north are officially blamed on rebels but rumoured to involve the army.
May 25 - Soldiers topple Kabbah and call for return of Sankoh, Musa and Bio.
